title: Shiproom Weekly Sync and Change Digest — 2025-11-04
notes:
Attendees: Aisha (chair), Javier, Maya, Liam, Priya, Samir, + SRE on-call (deferred). Quick stand; focus on pending change window on Friday and two incoming hotfixes.

Agenda:
- Review last week's change outcomes
- Hotfix queue and prioritization
- Rollout plan for v1.38.2 (model-serving runtime)
- Canary observations and metrics
- Known risks and mitigation

Summary / Highlights:
1) Friday change window confirmed 10:00–13:00 PDT. Targeted services: serving-runtime pool B, router v2, and cached-key invalidation. Deployment will be staged: canary on pool B, roll to pool A if no regressions in 30m.
2) Hotfix HOT-118 (KV-cache eviction bug) is priority 1. Javier to lead patch and coordinate with on-call. Expected deploy Tue morning after smoke validation.
3) RELENG-4921 (reduce default batch timeout for low-latency routes) merged to main; feature-flag rollout scheduled. Maya to monitor tail latencies.
4) Change log digest attached below; minor config flips and one migration for exporter metrics.

Change log summary (high level):
- infra: decrease batching timeout from 150ms -> 80ms for /v1/generate low-latency routes (RELENG-4921).
- serving-runtime: fix memory leak on attention cache eviction in quantized paths (HOT-118 candidate patch).
- router: opt-in region fallback policy for dedicated customers (PR#3241).
- observability: add rollout-specific spans for canary cohorts.

Hotfix queue (active, short descriptions):
- HOT-118: KV-cache eviction mis-indexes for long-lived sessions; reproduces with seq_len>4096. Owner: Javier Ortega. Target deploy: 2025-11-05 09:00 PDT.
- HOT-121: Model variant fallback returns stale weights for 2s after rollover. Owner: Priya Patel. In progress, blocked on integration tests.
- HOT-127: Billing meter double-count on retry loop in api-gateway. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Non-urgent, experimental rollback available.

Metrics / Canary observations (this week):
- Canary cohort (pool B) saw 12% p95 increase for long prompts after batching timeout change experiment; hypothesis points to client-side batching + server timeout interaction.
- Token-level cost decreased marginally for synthetic benchmark with new kernel selection.
- Error budget burn for region eu-west is 1.6% over 7d — keep watch; contains spikes tied to infra autoscaler.

Decisions made:
- Proceed with Friday change window; keep canary cohort at 10% traffic for first 30 minutes, then 50% for next 60 minutes, then full if green.
- HOT-118 will be cherry-picked and applied before the Friday window if smoke tests pass locally.
- If p95 latency increases >10% during canary versus baseline, automatic rollback will trigger and on-call will escalate to the shiproom channel.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: KV-cache fix has a chance to increase memory pressure for long-lived sessions. Mitigation: enable memory-limited eviction on canary nodes and watch RSS with alert threshold 85%.
- Risk: Batching timeout change might expose client SDKs that assume longer server timeouts. Mitigation: notify SDK team (Maya) and create compatibility test matrix; prepare guidance in SDK release note.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Javier: finish HOT-118 patch, add unit + repro test, open PR, and coordinate canary deploy. ETA 2025-11-05 08:00 PDT.
- Maya: run SDK compatibility matrix and share failing clients list; add to release notes. ETA 2025-11-06 EOD.
- Liam: prepare rollback image for router v2 and test toggles in staging. ETA 2025-11-05 12:00 PDT.
- Priya: unblock HOT-121 integration tests (info: race in variant loader); pair with infra team. ETA 2025-11-07.
- Samir: update shiproom runbook with Friday run order and communication checklist. ETA 2025-11-05 09:30 PDT.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Do we need to throttle client SDK batchers via server-side hints? (short-term workaround?)
- Should we create a temporary quota for long-sequence sessions to reduce risk? (deferred to SRE)
